Stale-event merge replay conformance for unknown fields is landed and pushed (revision 3f159eb on origin main). The generation conformance suite now exercises all three replay outcomes for the extension-bearing event. Idempotent replay - merging the log the destination restored from - must leave the stored extension map exactly as stored, asserted immediately before the later replays rewrite the same map. Widen - a newer producer replays the seeded future_tier value grown with nested shapes plus an additive future_tier_replayed key - must replace the stored map outright. Strip/narrow - a replay stripped of every additive field, the rendering of an older producer who never knew the keys - must leave the map exactly as the widen left it, via exact equality, so any erasure or value change fails. The negative half proves a would-be erasure fails the suite: dropping the seeded event key, dropping the widened key, and narrowing the widened value back to the older producer's all trip the preservation assertion by name. Verification ran on a clean git-archive extraction of the pushed HEAD with the target cache copied in - full definition-of-done (fmt, clippy all-targets -D warnings, full test suite) passed with 1564 tests green including all 3 tests of the conformance suite. A fleet checkpoint publish (6df14bf) landed on top afterward - .beads checkpoint files only, no source delta.

Pointer-level unknown-field corpus verified and gap-closed per the beadrs-e34d5ef4 split scope.

Verified already present from 4995a70: the record corpus seeds a distinct opaque key future_pointer_lineage with value {parents: [gen-1], gate: {sealed: false}} — array plus nested object — into .beads/checkpoint/current.json via seed_pointer_extension, and published_checkpoint_carries_unknown_fields_at_every_object_level asserts the next explicit flush re-projects it parse-equal (assert_pointer_level at generation 3). The restore/import leg is asserted by unknown_fields_survive_every_level_across_generations: seed in source, republish, sync import-only --restore-into-empty into an empty workspace, parse-equal staging in checkpoint_state.pointer_extensions_json, then re-projection on the generation 2 and 3 republishes. Test KNOWN_POINTER_KEYS (19 keys) match src/service/checkpoint.rs POINTER_KNOWN_KEYS exactly.

Gap closed by bd4a67a: the generation conformance suite pointer payload was scalar-only ({v: 1}) — the exact shape its own payload doc says cannot pass for preservation — so the restore-staging hop was only ever exercised with a scalar, and staging that flattened objects or dropped arrays would have passed unnoticed. The payload is now {lineage: [gen-1, gen-2], gate: {sealed: false}}, nested array and object in house payload style. Every assertion derives from pointer_extension_value, so one change covers the source republish, the restore staging, the generation 2/3 re-projections, and the deliberate-drop mutation.

Benefit: the current.json generation pointer is now provably tolerant of unknown extra JSON keys beside its known generation fields across flush and restore/import, with shapes a projection could flatten or stringify.

Steps 1-4 evidence: git status reviewed before staging — only tests/checkpoint_unknown_field_generation_conformance.rs was mine, the sibling staged .beads checkpoint churn was snapshotted, restored after landing, and preserved untouched. HEAD was extracted to /var/tmp/beadrs-6c62ae11-dod and the repository DoD ran there (not from the working tree), passing fmt + test. Named acceptance tests passed in that same clean extraction.
